posts.title: Why are AI agents lying, cheating and coordinating?
posts.author: jonifico
posts.description: A lot has been written about the incidents of the last few months in which AI agents misbehaved in serious ways. They took actions that would be considered as crimes if a human took them, escaped their containment to cheat on assigned tasks while attempting to evade detection, and coordinated toward goals nobody had specified, such as launching cyber attacks. Before concluding what to do about it, it is worth asking why.

posts.title: Apple's Siri AI Can Be Swapped Out for Claude, ChatGPT, Code Shows
posts.author: tosh
posts.description: Code sleuth "pdfu" has uncovered iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate private frameworks that show Apple has designed its new Siri architecture to work with third-party AI models at what appears to be a surprisingly deep level. One mechanism called Model Delegation allows Claude to appear as a Siri extension in the same way as the existing built-in ChatGPT extension.

posts.title: Dropping eBPF CPU Cost by About 90% with Memoization (Not AI Gen)
posts.author: nathannaveen
posts.description:
My brother and I spent a lot of time designing our eBPF security agent to be really fast from the ground up, but recently we discovered we could make it much faster using memoization!
A couple of weeks ago, I profiled the eBPF code and found that the most expensive part of the protection isn’t actually enforcing a policy (allow/deny), but figuring out which policy applies to a given file open.
